articles.title: Leonard Peltier on Indigenous Rights, His Half-Century in Prison & More
articles.content_excerpt: This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form. AMY GOODMAN : In this special broadcast, we spend the hour with longtime Indigenous activist Leonard Peltier. Last February, he was released from a federal prison in Florida after spending nearly half a century behind bars for a crime he says he did not commit. President Biden, on his last day in office, commuted Peltier’s life sentence to home confinement. Biden’s decision followed mounting calls by tribal leaders and supporters around the world in a decadeslong, community-led campaign fighting for his freedom. In the 1970s, Peltier was involved with the American Indian Movement, known as AIM . articles.title: A US court finds Huawei guilty of violating Iran sanctions and IP ‘theft’
articles.author: Abdul Rahman
articles.content_excerpt: A federal court in New York found Chinese technology and telecommunication giant Huawei and three of its subsidiaries guilty of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and commit bank fraud on Tuesday, November 24, while rejecting the more serious charges of “overarching racketeering” against it. The charge of “overarching racketeering,” was related to US allegations that Huawei was involved in secret operations to steal intellectual property or technological know-how from American companies. The trial in the case lasted for over two months with the jury finding Huawei guilty on 10 out of 12 charges. The sentencing is scheduled for September next year. articles.title: Rwanda deportation plan revived by five EU states after UK failure
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Five European Union states have announced plans to deport rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda from 2027, reviving a policy the United Kingdom spent two years and hundreds of millions of pounds on before scrapping it. Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece, and the Netherlands unveiled the scheme alongside Rwandan Interior Minister Vincent Biruta at the Vienna Migration Conference on November 16. In a joint statement , the governments said they are “jointly exploring” a return hub in Rwanda and aim to conclude an agreement and carry out the first transfers in 2027. As of now there is little information on the cost implications and the actual plan. articles.title: Israel’s targeted assassinations continue across Gaza despite the US-backed ceasefire
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: Israel escalated its aggression across the Gaza Strip during the last few days, carrying out targeted assassinations of senior Hamas officials and a United Nations employee. On Monday, November 23, an employee of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees (UNRWA) was killed in an Israeli drone strike while on duty in the Jabalia Refugee Camp in the northern Gaza Strip. On the same day, an Israeli warplane struck a civilian vehicle near Ansar Roundabout, west of Gaza City, killing three people and injuring several others.
